title: Reliability collaboration funnel playbook — rapid-adopter track
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, lightweight playbook for onboarding feature teams into our reliability program via a funneled rapid-adopter path. The goal is to reduce friction for small-to-medium feature launches (model endpoints and routes) while capturing signals to scale full SLO adoption. This doc is intentionally tactical and full of templates, not a canonical policy.

Audience:
- Primary: feature owners (product + eng) launching model-serving routes
- Secondary: platform, SRE, monitoring, and solutions engineering partners

High-level funnel (5 lanes) — quick summary:
1) Learn: outreach + discovery (1 week)
2) Prototype: quick integration with Redwood Console telemetry and basic SLIs (1–2 sprints)
3) Harden: define SLO(s), runbook, alert thresholds, and error-budget policy (2–4 sprints)
4) Validate: targeted experiments, canary traffic, and cost/latency tradeoff checks (2 sprints)
5) Graduate: handback to feature with steady-state ops and quarterly review cadence (ongoing)

Working definitions (shorthand used in this playbook):
- SLI: observable metric (p90 latency, success rate, token error rate)
- SLO: target for an SLI plus measurement window and burn policy
- Error budget: allowable deviation from SLO over rolling window

Success criteria for the rapid-adopter track: (must be measurable)
- Basic telemetry (request_count, success_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency) flowing into Redwood Console within 10 days of kickoff
- One documented SLO for the primary user-facing route before Beta launch
- Playbook runbook created and linked in team repo (on-call instructions, escalation steps)
- Less than 2 Sev2 incidents caused by missing instrumentation in the first 90 days post-launch

Phase-by-phase playbook (checklist + meeting rhythm)
1) Learn (kickoff + 1-week discovery)
- Kickoff invite: SRE + platform + feature owner (30–60m) — template below
- Output: short discovery note with target routes, expected QPS, latency targets, data sensitivity level
- Quick triage: decide whether rapid-adopter track is appropriate or full SLO program required

2) Prototype (integration sprint)
- Instrumentation checklist:
  - Add request-level tags (route, model_version, customer_tier)
  - Export metrics: request_count, error_count (separate transient vs permanent), latency_histogram
  - Add basic distributed trace spans for model loading, token generation, and encode/decode steps
- Tooling: ensure metrics visible in Console dashboard; set temporary dashboard share to SRE and feature owner
- Deliverable: ‘proto-dashboard’ link and short note with measurement gaps

3) Harden (SLO definition & runbook)
- Suggested SLO template: name, SLI definition (including success criteria and coverage), measurement window (rolling 30d), SLO target, escalation policy, owner
- Typical SLI candidates for model-serving: request_success_rate, user_observed_latency_p95, cost_per_1k_tokens (for economic guardrails)
- Runbook minimum: what to check first, how to ramp down traffic to fallbacks, contact matrix with escalation steps

4) Validate (experiments + canary)
- Canary plan template: traffic % ramp schedule, validation checks (latency, error rate, quality regressions), rollback criteria
- Rapid experiments: batch size/latency tradeoff, autotuning KV cache TTLs, quantization variant A/B test with cost comparison
- Validation docs: small evaluation prompt set and a quality baseline measurement captured pre- and post-change

5) Graduate (handoff + quarterly review)
- Handoff checklist: owner sign-off, SLO dashboard added to product weekly review, error budget dashboard subscription (owners + SRE)
- Quarterly review agenda: SLO compliance, alert noise analysis, cost per token trends, recommendations to optimize

RACI (lightweight)
- Feature owner: accountable for functional correctness, quality metrics, and sign-off
- SRE: accountable for SLO definition guidance, instrumentation review, and runbook pairing
- Platform/Console: responsible for dashboard setup, metric ingestion troubleshooting
- Solutions Eng / SE: responsible for customer-facing context and helping triage quality regressions

Example kickoff invite (copy-paste):
Subject: Kickoff — Reliability funnel: <feature-name> (week of YYYY-MM-DD)
Attendees: Feature owner (eng), Product PM, SRE partner (Jordan Kim), Platform eng lead, SE assigned
Agenda: 1) 10m context — product goals & launch timeline; 2) 20m capacity & architecture review; 3) 20m instrumentation plan & next steps
Output: Assigned owners for instrumentation, proto-dashboard link by EOD + 7 days

Telemetry & measurement tips (common gotchas)
- Don’t rely on aggregate percentiles alone for SLO gating — look at request volume distribution across customers
- Tagging matters: add customer_tier early so that heavy hitters don’t skew global SLOs
- Validate traces on synthetic requests (simple script) before depending on production traces for root cause analysis

Runbook snippet (copy into team docs):
- Symptom: sudden increase in p95 latency
  - Step 1: check recent deploys and model_version tags (5m)
  - Step 2: check GPU saturation / queue depth via platform metrics (5m)
  - Step 3: if latency > x ms and CPU/GPU at 90% -> shift a subset to fallback model or reduce batch size
  - Step 4: page SRE oncall if unable to mitigate within 15m

Open questions & quick notes to self:
- How quickly can platform expose per-model token-cost? (dependency on cost-export pipeline JIRA-3242)
- Need a lightweight way to capture quality regressions without full eval infra — propose small prompt-set harness maintained by SEs
- Consider a 'starter' SLO bundle for MLP teams: success_rate >= 99.5% rolling 30d + p95_latency <= 400ms

Low-friction templates attached (copy these into feature repo):
- Proto-dashboard JSON export (Console) — create and attach to ticket
- SLO definition markdown template
- Canary schedule table (simple CSV)

Immediate next actions (first two weeks) — owners shown in parens):
- Send kickoff invites (Jordan Kim)
- Run instrumentation smoke test and confirm metrics in Console (Elena Garcia)
- Create proto-dashboard and share with feature team (Platform Eng)
- Draft SLO proposal and post to feature repo for review (Ravi Menon)

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: teams treat SLOs as checkbox and don’t pair runbooks -> mitigation: require runbook for graduation
- Risk: dashboards aren't linked to oncall channels -> mitigation: platform to provide subscription template for owner + SRE

Appendix — quick links and examples:
- Example SLO (markdown):
  - name: user-visible-success
  - sli: fraction of requests returning 200-like user-facing responses (exclude client aborts)
  - window: rolling 30d
  - target: 99.9%
  - owner: @feature-team

- Example quick eval harness: small set of 50 prompts, run nightly against canary and baseline models, capture answer length, time-to-first-token, and failure rate. Store results in a shared CSV and link to dashboard.

If you're reviewing: please annotate the draft with missing tooling hooks you need (Console dashboards, trace spans, billing exports) and add any black-box quality checks you'd like to see in the validate phase. This doc is intentionally small — the funnel should cut work for feature teams, not add ceremony.
